h1: Beverly Hill Park Hotel Nakhon Sawan — a 3-star hotel on the Asia Highway built for the road trip
intro: If you're driving through Nakhon Sawan along the Asia Highway and want an easy place to park and rest for a night without going into town — Beverly Hill Park Hotel is a name road-trippers mention often. A 3-star, 106-room hotel on Ammarinwithee Road on the bypass side, with a leafy garden, free parking, a free shuttle and an on-site restaurant. It isn't a shiny new property, but measured by how convenient it is for drivers passing through — and a starting price of around ฿450/night — it earns its place.

body.html: What makes Beverly Hill Park Hotel a draw for travellers is its location right on the Asia Highway, on the bypass side. It sits on Ammarinwithee Road near Wat Khiriwong and the Nakhon Sawan Tower, with easy access on and off the main road — no need to thread through the lanes of downtown Pak Nam Pho. For anyone driving the long stretch from Bangkok up north and back, this is a stopover that's easy to find and easy to park at.

The hotel is a 3-star, 106-room property that has been around a while. What guests tend to praise is the leafy garden around the grounds and the quiet atmosphere, thanks to its setting away from the busy center. There's an on-site restaurant, the Mae-Ping Coffee Shop, handy for breakfast or a simple meal if you arrive late, plus free 24-hour parking and a free shuttle in some cases. It's a hotel that positions itself as a convenient stay rather than a destination in itself.

Rooms come in several tiers — ground-floor Deluxe with parking at the door, Lanna-style Premier on floors 2-3, VIP, Grand Deluxe, and Suite. Every room is air-conditioned with a TV, fridge, water heater and work desk. The ground-floor Deluxe rooms are popular with drivers because you can wheel your bags straight from the car into the room, while the Premier and VIP tiers feel a notch more finished, with carpeting and nicer décor than the basic rooms.
"Clean, spacious rooms at a budget price, with handy 24-hour parking and a quiet setting — a good place to break up a long drive."

To be honest, what reviews flag is the aging building and fittings. Some guests mention bathrooms that aren't cleaned into every corner, dated furniture and décor, and the occasional musty room if it hasn't been used recently. The overall Trip.com score sits around 6.2, which tells you this is a functional place to stay rather than one that will wow you on freshness.

Another thing to know before booking is that the bypass location trades driver convenience for a thin choice of restaurants nearby. Without a car, finding dinner at night or walking to sights is harder here than at a hotel in central Pak Nam Pho. A few reviews also mention slow check-in when it's busy. But with your own car, the drive into town is only a few minutes.

Overall, Beverly Hill Park Hotel scores around 6.2/10 on Trip.com (22 reviews) and 4.2/5 on TripAdvisor. It isn't the hotel I'd point a full-day Nakhon Sawan sightseer to, but if you're a driver passing through who wants easy parking, a quiet garden and a price starting around ฿450 that climbs to about ฿900 for higher room tiers — it does its job as an Asia Highway stopover.

A tip from reading the reviews: if you're driving, ask for a ground-floor Deluxe room with parking at the door — it's the most convenient. If you want a room in better shape, ask about the Premier or VIP tiers. Check the bathroom and the smell of the room on arrival, and ask to switch if it's not right. And bring dinner from town just in case, since options around the hotel are limited.

honestSummary: Beverly Hill Park Hotel is the right pick for drivers passing through Nakhon Sawan who want an easy stopover on the Asia Highway — free 24-hour parking, a quiet garden, and a starting price in the low hundreds of baht. The trade-off is an aging building and rooms, inconsistent cleanliness, and a bypass location with few options around it.
honestChecks: If you're here for a full day of sightseeing in Nakhon Sawan with no car — the bypass location has few restaurants around it and is hard to explore on foot → choose a hotel in central Pak Nam Pho within walking distance of malls and eateries instead.
If you care about a fresh, spotless room — the building and fittings are aging and some bathrooms aren't fully cleaned → ask for the Premier or VIP tier and check the room's condition on arrival.
If you're a driver wanting a one-night stopover — free 24-hour parking and easy Asia Highway access → ask for a ground-floor Deluxe room with parking at the door, the most convenient option.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Beverly Hill Park Hotel, Nakhon Sawan

faq.q: Where is Beverly Hill Park Hotel in Nakhon Sawan, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Beverly Hill Park Hotel is at 156/4 Moo 13, Ammarinwithee Road, Pak Nam Pho, on the Asia Highway bypass side. Wat Khiriwong is about a 5-minute drive and the Nakhon Sawan Tower about 7 minutes. It's easy on and off the main road, ideal as a road-trip stopover for drivers.

faq.q: How much does Beverly Hill Park Hotel cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿450/night for a ground-floor Deluxe room. Options range from Deluxe to Lanna-style Premier, VIP and Suite. Rates climb with the room tier to around ฿900-1,100 — always compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Beverly Hill Park Hotel have parking?
faq.a: Yes — free parking open 24 hours, and ground-floor Deluxe rooms let you park right at the door. It's the feature drivers passing through Nakhon Sawan like most, since you can wheel your bags straight from the car into the room.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Beverly Hill Park Hotel — are they clean?
faq.a: Rooms are air-conditioned with a TV, fridge, water heater and work desk. The building and fittings are aging, and some reviews mention bathrooms not cleaned into every corner or a musty smell. Ask for the Premier or VIP tier and check the room's condition on arrival.

faq.q: Who is Beverly Hill Park Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for drivers passing through Nakhon Sawan on the Asia Highway who want an easy stopover — free parking, a quiet garden, and budget pricing. It's less suited to car-free travellers wanting to explore town on foot, since the bypass location has few options nearby.

faq.q: Are there restaurants near Beverly Hill Park Hotel?
faq.a: There's an on-site restaurant, the Mae-Ping Coffee Shop, good for breakfast or a simple meal. But options around the hotel are limited because it's on the bypass side. If you arrive late, it's worth picking up dinner from Pak Nam Pho town.
